To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ciliary membrane contains anionic sites that are distributed in a characteristic manner on its surface and that the anionic sites are associated with special membrane modifications in two distinct regions of the ciliary membrane.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of anionic sites in the membrane of ciliated epithelium of the oviduct of the golden hamster.
the distribution of the anionic sites on ciliary membranes.
the structure of the oviduct epithelium and the function of its cilia in the transport of spermatozoa and other materials from the uterus to the ampullary isthmus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ciliary membrane of the oviduct is a mosaic surface containing a variety of anionic sites.
anionic sites on ciliary membranes are localized to a specialized glycocalyx at the tip of the cilia and to a series of ridges around the transition region.
the anionic sites on ciliary membranes are distributed along the length of cilia in a pattern of alternating regions of high and low anionic charge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution of PCF-binding sites on the ciliary membrane is nonuniform, being concentrated at the base of the transition region and at the tip of the cilia.
the distribution of anionic sites is nonuniform and is correlated with the distribution of the special surface modifications of ciliary membrane.
the ciliary membrane is not uniform in composition, but rather has a number of specialized regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ciliary membrane of the mammalian oviduct is a highly modified structure with specialized surface components that are not found in other ciliary systems.

the oviduct epithelium contains a variety of surface glycoproteins and mucopolysacchardies, which are differentially exposed on the surface of the ciliary membrane and may play a role in sperm transport and fertilization.
PCF is a useful visual probe for anion sites on the ovoiduct ciliary membrane and that the distribution of these sites on the membrane surface is not uniform.
